Per medication, this output should all go in a single cell of a table. The output should include a table with one column and one row per medication that can be easily copied and pasted into a CSV file.

Please recommend changes or additions to their diabetes medications. Please output one row per medication. If the medication dose or frequency is being changed, describe the change and the final dose and frequency. If the medication is being continued without change, say so and give the continued dose and frequency. If the medication is being stopped note this. If a new medication is being added, give the name of the medication and the dose and frequency. If titration is planned in the next few months, please simply state that the medication will be titrated up. For rapid acting insulin regimens, please summarize the dosing schedule concisely but it is fine to take 2-3 lines of text if needed. Do NOT give contingency plans or choices between several options. We need the patient to walk out with a single plan to implement. ONLY provide recommendations for antihyperglycemic drugs - no vitamins, blood pressure medications, lipid lowering medications, for example. Per medication, this output should all go in a single cell of a table. The output should include a table with one column and one row per medication that can be easily copied and pasted into a CSV file.

Patient Vignette:

Her medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, and recurrent urinary tract infections. BMI is 34 kg/m2 and blood pressure is 138/82 mmHg. Labs: HbA1c 8.4%, fasting glucose 188 mg/dL, eGFR 72 mL/min/1.73m2, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, urine albumin-creatinine ratio 38 mg/g, total cholesterol 202 mg/dL, HDL 46 mg/dL, LDL 118 mg/dL, triglycerides 212 mg/dL. She is a former smoker who quit 12 years ago. Current medications include losartan and simvastatin.
